headline_hook: Cloudflare Ships Ephemeral Agent Accounts as a Startup Claims It Cracked the Attention Wall

pick_of_the_day.thesis: Whether or not Subquadratic's claim holds up, the fact that a small team is publicly challenging a decade-old architectural constraint tells us the transformer efficiency frontier is now a startup race — and the incumbents training ever-larger quadratic models may be building on borrowed time.

model_literacy.relevance: Today's Subquadratic story claims to solve the O(n²) cost of self-attention — the mechanism that makes every token attend to every other token. This is why doubling context length quadruples compute, and why 'long context' models are expensive to run. Understanding this bottleneck explains why a true subquadratic solution would reshape model scaling economics.

items.title: Cloudflare Introduces Throwaway Accounts Built for AI Agents
items.angle: The infrastructure layer is now designing for AI-first tenancy — ephemeral, scoped credentials that treat agents as first-class operators, not users with API keys
items.key_fact: Agents get short-lived Cloudflare accounts with scoped permissions instead of permanent API keys
